subject: POC trial environment - setup & success criteria
messages: From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Subject: Recap & next steps — POC trial environment options
Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and lots of alignment on what success looks like for Avatech's fraud-checking workflow. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the POC plan:
1) Goal / success criteria (as discussed):
- Latency: median p95 < 250ms for 512-token inference during peak test window
- Accuracy: match or exceed current heuristic pass-rate on labeled test set (we'll formalize with a shared eval set),
- Cost: target token cost <= $0.002/token for production-like throughput (we'll measure during POC),
- Stability: sustained 2k reqs/min for 30 minutes with <1% error rate.
2) POC environment options (tradeoffs):
- Hosted sandbox (fastest): Redwood-hosted trial API; quickest to onboard but not ideal for large-scale throughput tests or data isolation needs.
- Dedicated sandbox (recommended): Dedicated GPU pool reserved for Avatech for the POC; gives realistic throughput/latency and avoids noisy-neighbor effects.
- VPC trial (most restrictive): Private VPC/private control plane for customers requiring strict network controls; takes longer to provision and requires network config on your side.
3) Suggested plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria + sign mutual action plan (attached POC-MAP.xlsx),
- Week 1: if Dedicated sandbox chosen — Redwood provisions dedicated pool; SE kickoff and account access,
- Weeks 2–3: ingest sample data, run baseline perf tests and iterate on prompts/config,
- Week 4: formal evaluation window + review and go/no-go decision.
4) Ownership:
- Redwood: provisioning, SE support (Dylan), baseline tests, monitoring dashboards
- Avatech: provide eval dataset, expected throughput profiles, security/compliance contacts for SOC2 evidence
Dylan — can you confirm the provisioning lead times for a dedicated sandbox and list the network/prereq items we should ask Avatech to prepare?
Sam / Priya — please confirm which environment you want to pursue (Dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial vs Hosted) and whether the timeline above looks achievable.
Attaching POC-MAP.xlsx with a proposed mutual action plan. I also attached a short SOC2 checklist so you can see what evidence we can share during the POC.
Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — POC trial environment options
Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Success criteria: we'll formalize an eval set (Priya will own) and share expected throughput matrix (burst vs sustained). The latency and stability targets look right.

- Environment preference: we prefer a Dedicated sandbox for the initial POC so we can run throughput tests that reflect production behavior. VPC trial is something we may request later if the POC proves out and legal wants network isolation.
- Timeline: 4–6 weeks is fine; leaning to a 6-week window to allow for data prep and internal security review.
- Security evidence: Priya will run our security checklist across your SOC2 and will ask for any additional artifacts — sending the questionnaire separately.

We'll need a short statement of what data is logged/retained in the sandbox and where logs/audit trails are accessible. Can you confirm retention defaults and whether logs can be exported to our Splunk instance?
Sam

Hi all — happy to take this. High-level answers and a short pre-provisioning checklist below.
Provisioning lead times (Dedicated sandbox):
- Once mutual action plan + AAD/ID provisioning info received: ~3 business days to allocate GPUs, configure model variants, and open account-level routes.
- VPC trial: typically 2–3 weeks (network reviews + firewall rules + certs).
Default logs & retention:
- Control plane events: retained 90 days by default (can be extended as an add-on),

- Request/response audit logs: retained 30 days in the trial environment; we can stream to a customer SIEM (Splunk) via our secure log export integration. We will provide a short config guide for Splunk ingestion.
Pre-provisioning checklist (what we need from Avatech):
1) Shared eval dataset (S3 link or secure upload) and expected throughput profile (CSV),
2) List of IP ranges for egress/inbound (if you choose VPC or IP allow-listing),
3) Point of contact for IAM/service account provisioning (email + minimal IAM role),
4) Security contact for SOC2 artifact exchange (Priya).
Estimated timeline for tests:
- Day 0–3 after access: baseline smoke tests and small-scale perf runs,
- Day 4–10: full throughput tests and tuning (prompt changes, batching),
- Week 2–3: formal evaluation window and metric collection.
Ownership and single points of contact:
- Redwood SE (Dylan) — provisioning, instrumenting dashboards, running initial perf runs,
- Redwood AM (Marissa) — commercial coordination, credit approvals, and roadmap syncs,
- Avatech Eng (Sam) — dataset and throughput profiles,
- Avatech Security (Priya) — SOC2 questionnaire and evidence requests.
I'll attach a short network config template (used internally) to help your networking team — Dylan
